title.narrative: Acts/Crimes of solidarity: an ethnographic study of illegalisation and criminalisation amongst pro-migration activists and other citizens

description.narrative: Research and development activity contributing to the UK’s strategy to address key development challenges.

The project has been co-designed and will be co-delivered with two international Project Partners: GADEM and PSMigrants. GADEM (Groupe Antiraciste de Défense et d'Accompagnement des Etrangers et Migrants, or the Antiracist Collective of Advocacy and Support for Foreigners and Migrants) was established in 2006 by migration activists and researchers in Morocco. GADEM produces regular reports to monitor practices and policies on migration and human rights and delivers capacity building for other organisations. GADEM takes an active part in national and international networks, (e.g. Migreurop, a Euro-African network on migration). PSMigrants (Plateforme de Service aux Migrant.e.s, or Migrants' Support Platform) is a network set up in 2011 by local (e.g. L'Auberge des Migrants), national (e.g. Cimade) and international (e.g. Doctors without borders) civil society organisations working on migration in the northern French region Hauts-de-France and along the Channel French coastline. The platform exchanges resources, knowledge, skills, practices and experiences to enhance the defence of migrants' rights. It supports civil society organisations in advocacy work, including building awareness amongst decision-makers, the media and the wider public about migration issues, compiling reports, and developing legal actions. The partnerships with GADEM and PSMigrants will be crucial to: 1) foster collaboration with other research projects on migration in Morocco and France; 2) facilitate access to other organisations and activists (including foreign activists such as British citizens in northern France) in the two field sites for research; 3) to enhance the impact of the project beyond academia through the co organisation and co-delivery of impact activities and the dissemination of outputs via their extended networks
